rationale: Recovery/context-validity question on hashicorp/raft: after a node restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, does its in-memory configuration still reflect the committed configuration entries retained in its own log? NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct and only two producers can supply it before the run loop starts: restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681, the latest snapshot's configuration) and the startup log scan at api.go:610-613. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(persisted) + processLogs(persisted), i.e. it advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index. The scan then starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastappliedIndex)+1, so every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is skipped; processLogs never touches r.configurations (prepareLog only forwards LogConfiguration to the FSM). Consequence: the node's configuration view reverts to the snapshot's configuration, or to the empty configuration when no snapshot exists, even though its own log holds a committed LogConfiguration. A native construction probe (single node, CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries, restart) produced after_latest_index=0 / after_servers=0 / after_has_vote=false with the flag on and after_latest_index=1 / after_servers=1 / after_has_vote=true with the flag off, logging 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'. That probe is construction feedback only, not a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment re-establishes both cases under controller execution. Counterevidence considered: the snapshot path can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678) but only up to snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, so it cannot cover configuration entries committed after the snapshot; appendEntries processes configuration entries only among the new entries it appends (raft.go:1594-1621) so an already-present entry is not replayed; leaderLoop only marks an already-known latest configuration as committed (raft.go:797-799). Limits: the snapshot-present variant is argued from source but not yet witnessed and is registered as a gap; a second, distinct suspicion (restoreFromCommittedLogs calling processLogs before runFSM starts, fsmMutateCh buffered at 128 batches) is untested and is not part of this claim.

investigations.question: After a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, is the node's in-memory configuration still the committed configuration retained in its own log?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup configuration scan, so the scan bound max(snapshotIndex, lastappliedIndex)+1 skips committed LogConfiguration entries and r.configurations keeps the snapshot (or empty) value.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same single-node state twice from identical stores, once with RestoreCommittedLogs on and once off, and compare configuration index, server count and hasVote(local) observed immediately after NewRaft returns; the cases differ only in whether lastApplied was advanced by restoreFromCommittedLogs.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the persisted commit index from GetCommitIndex is at least the index of the latest committed LogConfiguration entry; no snapshot covers that entry (no snapshot at all, or snapshot.ConfigurationIndex below it).

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: The retained receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f (exit 0) contains the four emitted events, and the two result events witness the predicted difference under identical inputs: event 1 (mode on, restore_committed_logs true, snapshots 0) reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false with after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, while event 3 (mode off) reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1, after_has_vote true. The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Source reading explains the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped, and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The receipt s declared comparisons returned unknown rather than violated: the controller reported "No corresponding prerequisite events reached: mode_on/startup_before_restart" for both on-case comparisons and the analogous message for the off-case control, because the compared identity included phase and the admission events carry phase before_restart while the result events carry after_restart. That is a declaration defect, not missing evidence, so the raw observations are retained and a successor experiment with identity_fields [mode] is submitted for a fresh, complete comparison; no completed comparison is claimed here. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node holds an empty (or snapshot-age) membership view, so runFollower's "no known peers, aborting election" branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) leave it unable to campaign, and quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) is computed over a configuration that contradicts its own committed log.
counterevidence: A restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration (event 3), which isolates the flagged recovery path rather than the restart itself.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot.
limitations: The comparison outcomes in this receipt are unknown; a completed comparison waits on the successor experiment.
Only the single-node, no-snapshot case is witnessed; the snapshot-present variant remains the registered gap.
The separate suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts is untested and outside this claim.

scope.description: Bootstrap a single-node cluster whose LogStore is a CommitTrackingLogStore, commit ten commands (leaving the bootstrap LogConfiguration at index 1 committed), shut the node down without any snapshot, restart it from the identical logs/stable/snapshots stores and emit the configuration observed immediately after NewRaft returns. Run the identical sequence twice, with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and false.
assumptions: The in-memory commit-tracking store stands in for a durable CommitTrackingLogStore per the interface contract in log.go:194-219.
No snapshot is taken, so the snapshot path cannot supply a configuration.
Restarting a one-node configuration is a legal deployment of the library; the difference between the two cases is only whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied.
excluded: Whole-package or repository test suites; only the two named cases run.
Any snapshot-present scenario, which is left to the registered gap.
The separate suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts.

experiment.prefix: The harness uses the package's own test facilities: inmemConfig, MakeClusterOpts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} and MakeClusterCustom, so BootstrapCluster writes the LogConfiguration entry at index 1 and NewRaft runs the real startup path. SnapshotThreshold/SnapshotInterval/TrailingLogs are raised so no snapshot exists. Ten Apply calls are awaited, then the node is Shutdown and NewRaft is called again with the same logs, stable and snapshots stores and a fresh inmem transport, as the package's own restart test does. The event is emitted after NewRaft returns; no leader-dependent step is assumed at restart time. The harness first emits a startup_before_restart event describing the committed configuration index and server count observed before shutdown (the setup the result event depends on), then the restart_after_recovery result event; both events carry the same mode/phase identity so the two cases stay distinguishable.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the precondition that a node's in-memory configuration reflects the committed configuration in its own log at startup; the caller only selects Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and supplies a CommitTrackingLogStore.

comparisons.description: With RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, the restarted node's latest configuration index is expected to equal the committed configuration index observed before the restart (1); the defect prediction is that it is 0.
The restarted node's configuration is expected to contain itself as a voter; the defect prediction is that it does not.
Control: with RestoreCommittedLogs off the same restart is expected to keep the committed configuration (index 1, one voter), isolating the flagged recovery path as the cause.

experiment.revision_reason: Only the comparison declaration changes: identity_fields are reduced to the case selector (mode) so the startup_before_restart admission and the restart_after_recovery result share an identity; the harness, inputs and assertions are unchanged. The previous receipt correlated neither admission to a result, so its comparisons returned unknown even though the raw events were emitted.
